english.title: Wildlife - uproot a wild plant
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), not being an authorised person, intentionally uprooted

(A)_[a wild plant,]_
(B)_[wild plants,]_

namely **(..SPECIFY SPECIES..)
english.legislation: Contrary to section 13(1)(b) and 21(1) of the Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) See Section 21(7) for place where offence deemed to have been committed for jurisdiction purposes.
(ii) Section 21(5) provides that where more than one plant is involved in a single offence the maximum fine shall be determined as if the person convicted had been convicted of a separate offence in respect of each.
(iii) See Section 13(3) for defence.
(iv) See Section 27 for meaning of "uproot" and "wild plant".
(v) See Section 20 for time limit for prosecutions involving the picking, uprooting or destruction of any wild plant.
(vi) As amended by paragraph 10 of Schedule 12 to the Countryside and Rights of Way Act 2000.
(vii) See Section 21(6) for the forfeiture provisions.

other.penalty:
Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale

Where more than one plant is involved in a single offence the maximum fine shall be determined as if the person convicted had been convicted of a separate offence in respect of each plant (Section 21(5)).

Time limit for prosecutions:
Complex - see legislation
